meta.name: Review GitHub PR security with DeepSeek and Gmail alerts

options.systemMessage:
Act as a senior security and code reviewer. You will be given a pull request's title, author, repository, and diff.

Analyze the diff for: hardcoded secrets, API keys, or passwords, SQL injection risk, unsafe eval/exec usage, missing input validation, insecure auth logic, overly broad permissions, obvious logic bugs, missing error handling.

Determine an overall verdict (pass, needs_changes, or blocked), list every specific issue found with its file, an approximate line number in the file where the issue occurs (integer, best estimate from the diff hunk headers), severity, and a short description, and write a 2-3 sentence summary of your findings.

Base your analysis only on the actual diff content provided. Do not invent issues that aren't present in the diff.

Your response must strictly follow the structured output format required by the system. Do not return markdown or prose.

nodes.name: 10. Post Inline Comments on Flagged Lines

parameters.content:
## 🤖 Automated GitHub PR Security & Code Reviewer

This workflow turns every pull request into an instantly-reviewed one. The moment a PR opens or updates, AI analyzes the diff for security and code issues, then reports back on GitHub itself and by email, no one has to remember to run a manual security pass.

### 🧩 Why This Isn't Just Another Linter
Most automated PR checks (CodeQL, linters, test runners) only catch known rule-based patterns. This workflow instead:
• Uses an LLM to reason about context, not just pattern-match, catching things like a hardcoded secret OR invalid syntax mixed into the wrong file type
• Anchors feedback to the exact diff position, not a guessed file line, so inline comments always land on the right line
• Posts a real GitHub commit status (not just a comment), so it can become an enforced merge gate, not just advice someone can ignore
• This combination took inline comment accuracy from "guessed line, often wrong" to reliably correct by parsing the actual diff hunk positions

### 🔍 What It Does
This workflow:
• Triggers on every PR opened or updated (synchronize)
• Fetches the full diff and sends it to an AI reviewer
• Posts a pass/needs_changes/blocked commit status check on the PR
• Posts a summary comment with the verdict and every issue found
• Posts individual inline comments directly on each flagged line
• Emails the relevant verdict-specific report so nothing gets missed

### ⚙️ How It Works
• GitHub Trigger fires on pull_request events, filtered to opened/synchronize only
• The PR diff is fetched and formatted (truncated if huge) for the AI
• An AI Agent reviews it against a structured checklist (secrets, injection risk, unsafe eval, missing validation, broken auth, logic bugs, missing error handling) and returns a strict JSON verdict
• A commit status check posts immediately based on the verdict
• A summary comment posts, then each issue is mapped to its real diff position and posted as an inline comment
• A Switch node routes to one of three email notifications based on the final verdict

### 💪 Key Capabilities
• Structured, enforced JSON output (verdict, severity-tagged issues, summary), not free-form prose
• Diff-position-aware inline commenting, computed from the real diff text, not guessed
• Real GitHub status check integration, can be wired into branch protection to actually block merges
• Three-way verdict routing (blocked / needs_changes / pass) with tailored notifications for each
• Advisory by design: a human always makes the final merge call, this only removes the guesswork

### 📦 Requirements
• GitHub fine-grained PAT with: Pull requests (R/W), Contents (Read-only), Metadata (Read-only), Webhooks (R/W), Commit statuses (R/W)
• AI model credential (DeepSeek used here, swap for any OpenAI-compatible provider)
• Gmail account for notifications (or swap for Slack, same routing applies)
• (Recommended) GitHub branch protection rule requiring the "ai-pr-reviewer" status check

### 💡 Example Use Cases
• Small teams/startups without a dedicated security reviewer on every PR
• Citizen-developer / low-code automation programs where non-engineers are shipping workflows with live API access
• Open-source repos needing a consistent first-pass review before a maintainer's time is spent
• Any team wanting a documented, auditable trail of what was flagged and why on every merge

## 📧 Notifications
One branch per verdict: blocked / needs changes / passed.

Swap these Gmail nodes for Slack (or both) if you prefer chat-based alerts — same routing, just a different output node.

## Trigger & filter incoming PRs

Fires on every pull_request event, then filters down to only 'opened' or 'synchronize' so a fresh push gets re-reviewed without re-triggering on every PR event type (labels, comments, etc).

## Fetch and prepare the diff

Pulls the raw unified diff for the PR, attaches PR title/author/repo metadata, and truncates it if huge so it fits cleanly inside the AI's context window.

## AI review with structured output

An AI Agent reviews the diff against a security + code quality checklist. The Structured Output Parser enforces a strict verdict/issues/summary JSON shape, including a line number per issue, used later to place inline comments.

## Post status check & summary comment

Immediately posts a pass/fail commit status to GitHub, then posts one overview comment on the PR listing the verdict and every issue found.

## Map & post inline comments

Skips cleanly if no issues were found. Otherwise parses the real diff text to compute each issue's exact diff position, then posts a review comment directly on that line.

issues.description: Hardcoded API key 'sk-test-1234567890abcdef' added to the source file. Even though it appears to be a fake/test value, committing secret-looking credentials to the repository is a security anti-pattern and could be mistaken for or reused as a real credential; it should be removed and stored in an environment variable or secret manager.

JavaScript syntax ('const apiKey = ...') was inserted into a Python file at the top level outside any function, which will raise a SyntaxError if the module is executed/imported, breaking the application.

output.summary: This PR intentionally adds a hardcoded secret-looking API key and invalid JavaScript syntax to the end of a Python file, which introduces both a security risk and a runtime-breaking syntax error. The change should be blocked and the added lines removed entirely.
